items.suggested_action: Before planning a session block, pick the character the block's activities belong to, and stay on them. Switching characters mid-block loses same-colour '?' blips and can invalidate the plan.
items.avoid: Driving Michael to the hunting ground or Trevor to Hao's start line. Avoid earning shooting-range medals on one character and expecting the discount on another.
items.exceptions: Tennis protagonist restrictions are contested between sources (see the tennis item).

items.cue: the agent's state shows wanted level > 0 while heading to a shop, race marker, or activity.
items.context: All shops and activity markers.
items.meaning: A wanted level blocks entry to shops (Ammu-Nation, clothing, barbers) and prevents activity markers from triggering. Los Santos Customs is the exception and the tool: entering resprays the vehicle and clears the wanted level, provided police lost visual contact on the way in. Riding a freight train into a tunnel also sheds stars.
items.suggested_action: Clear the wanted level FIRST — nearest Los Santos Customs (Burton, La Mesa, LSIA, Harmony) or a train tunnel — then resume the goal. Treat 'clear stars' as an explicit prerequisite step in any plan involving a shop or marker.
items.avoid: Repeatedly driving into an activity marker with stars up and reporting that the activity is broken. Avoid entering LSC with a police helicopter directly overhead.
items.exceptions: The line-of-sight rule for LSC is described qualitatively by the source and its exact detection behaviour should be tested on the real machine.

notes:
SOURCES AND METHOD
Primary sources fetched: gta.wiki (a GTA Wiki mirror, both /wiki/ and /w/ path forms) for ~25 article-level facts, and gtabase.com for the side-mission overview and the stunt jump guide. gta.fandom.com was not used (402 to this fetcher, per the brief). The WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted mid-task (200/200), so later verification was done by fetching gta.wiki's Special:Search endpoint directly and by URL-guessing article titles; a few articles resolved only to disambiguation pages and had to be re-fetched at their (HD Universe) titles.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY
1. Coordinates. I deliberately included NO map coordinates. None of the sources gave usable in-game world coordinates, and inventing them would give the agent's drive_to a plausible-looking wrong number. Every location here is named by district/street. The harness must resolve these to coordinates once on the real machine and write them back.
2. Single-player helicopter spawn points. This is the weakest item in the set (confidence: low). The gta.wiki Maverick article explicitly declines to list story-mode free-roam helipad spawns and its spawn data is GTA Online rank-gated. The one confirmed SP route is hijacking the green Maverick at a parachute-jump marker. Must be established empirically.
3. Unique vehicles. The Duke O'Death article conflates story mode and Online (it quotes a Warstock price, which is an Online mechanic). Space Docker acquisition unverified. All marked low confidence.
4. Epsilon Program details. The gta.wiki article resolved only to a disambiguation page and the WebSearch budget was gone; I kept the item but at medium confidence with donation amounts and step order flagged as unverified.
5. Rampage specifics. The dedicated Rampage article 404'd; the count of five comes only from the Strangers and Freaks index.
6. Ad-hoc parachute purchase at Ammu-Nation is widely reported but was not confirmed in either fetched Ammu-Nation source; flagged medium.

SOURCE DISAGREEMENTS (all flagged in the items' `exceptions`)
- Tennis: gta.wiki says 8 courts and claims only Michael and Trevor play as primary characters; gtabase/sportskeeda say 9 courts and imply all three. Unresolved.
- Yoga and 100%: gtabase lists yoga as OPTIONAL (in its 19 optional hobbies); other coverage treats it as required. gta.wiki's own 100% checklist does not list it. I recorded the disagreement rather than picking a side.
- Under the Bridge distribution: gta.wiki says "Los Santos: 10 bridges" while describing the canals as the main cluster — internally inconsistent and inconsistent with community counts. The total (50) and the 100% threshold (25) are solid; the regional split is not.
- Knife flights: gta.wiki's per-district list sums to 14, not the stated 15.
- Mount Chiliad height: 797.1m in-game vs a claimed 2,744m in-universe, in the same article. I used the in-game figure.
- Stock car racing: gta.wiki says it is exclusive to enhanced versions for players who previously owned PS3/360 copies. If true on the installed build, the Marshall monster truck goal is unavailable. gtabase lists it as a normal optional hobby with no such caveat.
- LSIA access: the claim that Michael and Franklin have free tarmac access "from the beginning of the game" is tied to a post-launch update and comes from one source; the baseline 3-star trespass rule is the safer assumption.

DELIBERATE OMISSIONS
Nothing GTA Online-only was included as if it were story mode. Two Online mechanics that appeared in otherwise-relevant articles are explicitly called out as NOT applying: buying a Fort Zancudo hangar for legitimate base access (2017 Online feature), and the Warstock purchase route for the Duke O'Death.

ONE HARNESS-SIDE NOTE
Several of the highest-value cues here ("a green '?' blip appears", "a random event marker appears nearby", "an activity marker is within 300m") depend on the harness exposing NEARBY MAP BLIPS in game state, not just the single active objective blip. As specified in the brief, the agent only receives an objective blip when the game exposes one. Without a nearby-blip list, roughly a third of these items degrade from reactive cues to timed/scheduled goals, and the random-events item — which I rate as the single best source of unscripted watchable moments — becomes largely unusable. Worth raising with whoever owns the bridge's state payload.

REPAIR PASS (against CAPABILITIES.md + 2 critic findings)
Applied: (1) lsia_three_stars rewritten — the 'Michael/Franklin free tarmac access' claim is now framed as unconfirmed (re-verified against gta.wiki, which itself contradicts whether it's even a Story Mode mechanic), default assumption is 3 stars for all three protagonists; fixed_wing_acquisition's cross-reference updated to match. (2) The stuck-detection/no-displacement loop-risk finding does not apply to this file — grepped for 'construction_accident', 'ram', 'push', 'winch', 'trailer'-as-obstacle and stuck-detector config: none exist here: rejected as not applicable, not fixed. (3) Removed two explicit special-ability violations (Franklin's 'time-slowing driving ability' as a suggested_action) in stunt_jumps_50 and goal_aqueduct_stunt_run, and added a 'this ability isn't available to the agent' clarifier to the two freight-train items that mention Trevor's special ability as a factual game exception. (4) Identified and fixed a file-wide, previously-unflagged class of capability violation: 'no parachute deploy' is explicit in CAPABILITIES.md, which blocks EVERY item in the parachuting category and four fun_goal items (goal_maze_bank_bike_jump, goal_turbine_terror, goal_moving_target_landings, goal_chiliad_descent's parachute alt) — rewrote all six to state plainly that the agent cannot deploy a chute, so any height jump is a fatal fall, not a stunt; updated goal_selection_heuristic so it no longer recommends parachute jumps as a good pick. (5) Removed commanded manual-aim/fire/weapon-select/melee actions (all explicitly banned) from hunting_trevor_daylight, goal_hunting_trip (heart/head shots), goal_bail_bond_manhunt (stun gun/takedown), and ammunation_shooting_ranges (medal grinding requires aim); reframed each around what the agent can actually do or marked the activity as an atmosphere-only visit. (6) Softened golf/tennis/darts suggested_actions — these need analog aim/power/timing input the agent's vocabulary doesn't have — to 'visit, don't narrate completion'; kept yoga as-is since its QTEs are single contextual prompts press_prompt_key can plausibly drive, but added a note that the agent has no way to fight off a Mount Gordo cougar attack. (7) helicopter_acquisition_singleplayer's 'hold vs tap to hijack' instruction rewritten — enter_nearest_vehicle has no such parameter, so that behavior is the bridge's to decide, not the agent's to choose. No items deleted; all 58 ids preserved.
